title: Actual compact-support localization arrows and coefficient boundary normalization
statement: Fix a six-functor push stage P as in [def-sf-operation-stages], a closed i:Z→X with complementary open j:U→X, f:X→Y and compactifications c,cj,ci. Define the actual open and closed vertex comparisons by composition followed by open identification or proper coincidence. The first arrow is the image of the open counit through its comparison; the second is the image of the closed unit through its comparison. A boundary is a natural transformation from the actual closed value to the shift by one of the actual open value. The localization triangle uses these first two arrows and the boundary. The realization predicate identifies its boundary with every distinguished source completion through the specified realization and shift maps. For a coefficient comparison, the outer vertex comparison is support comparison followed by the image of pullback comparison, and the boundary condition is the third square with the prescribed shift. For an integral higher stage H, the tower-boundary predicate pins the integral boundary to the designated strict tower, normalized projections, exact image triangle, natural support comparison and composite shift; the rational-boundary predicate records an integral tower boundary, its rationalization square and rational distinguishedness. Finally, the field-system predicate uses one family at all finite coefficient fields, with common-stage distinguishedness and its inclusion and scalar-transition boundary squares. These are precisely the existing definitions, moved from the realization module with identical bodies; the boundary type is an ordinary definition instead of an abbreviation so proofs can keep its large category expression folded locally.
